x: The UNDP published the first Human Development Report in 1990. OPHI works with the UNDP on the Multidimensional Poverty Index.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: Option C is incorrect: GDP is a one-dimensional measure of income and output. Capabilities and well-being are the focus of the human development approach.
t: Discriminate GDP from human development.

x: Option D is incorrect: human development is a broad, people-centred approach about opportunities and choices. Focusing only on income and output describes GDP.
t: Watch for 'only' narrowing the scope.

x: Both are true: the human development approach is broader than an economic measure because it looks at people, their opportunities and their choices, not just output. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the focus explains the breadth.

x: Both are true: Sen's capability approach is the foundation of human development, and the approach focuses on capabilities and well-being. That the approach shares Sen's focus does not show it was built on his work, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a shared focus proves the origin.

x: Both are true: GDP measures one thing, income, while human development is a multidimensional approach centred on people.
t: Discriminate GDP from human development.

x: A is true and B is false: the MPI measures multidimensional poverty, but it is produced by OPHI and UNDP together, not UNDP alone.
t: Watch for 'alone'.

x: All three are correct: Mahbub-ul-Haq built the human development approach on Amartya Sen's capability approach, and the first Human Development Report came out in 1990.
t: Recall the origins of the HDR.

x: Mahbub-ul-Haq developed the approach, Sen gave the capability approach, the UNDP published the first report, and OPHI with the UNDP produces the MPI. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each name to its contribution.

x: GDP is mainly an economic measure, human development a broader people-centred approach, the HDI measures human development, and the MPI multidimensional poverty. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each measure to its description.

x: The first HDR came out in 1990, the MPI was first included in the 2010 HDR, the UNDP publishes the HDR, and the MPI measures multidimensional poverty. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate 1990 from 2010.

x: Three are HDI dimensions: health (life expectancy), education and standard of living. Income and output on their own are GDP's focus.
t: Recall the three HDI dimensions.

x: I, II and III are correct: the HDI measures human development, the MPI multidimensional poverty, and both use health, education and living standards. IV is false because GDP is the mainly economic measure.
t: Discriminate HDI from GDP.

x: Both are true: the HDI is produced by the UNDP and published in its Human Development Report.
t: Recall the HDI's publisher.

x: Infrastructure development is a requirement for inclusive growth because it widens access and economic opportunity. The other options are roles or sectors, not the listed requirement.
t: Discriminate requirements from roles.

x: In inclusive growth, infrastructure widens access and economic opportunities. Credit enables productive activity, and education improves capabilities.
t: Match each factor to its role.

x: Reviving agriculture mainly helps the rural population, since most rural people depend on farming.
t: Match each factor to its beneficiary.

x: Education improves capabilities. Health improves human capital, and credit enables productive activity.
t: Discriminate capabilities from human capital.

x: Health improves human capital. Education improves capabilities, and infrastructure widens opportunities.
t: Discriminate capabilities from human capital.

x: Option C is incorrect: SHGs promote financial and economic participation. Improving human capital is the role of health.
t: Match each factor to its role.

x: Option C is incorrect: inclusive governance includes planning and welfare services, along with equal access to government facilities and participation.
t: Watch for 'excludes'.

x: Both are true: infrastructure is needed for inclusive growth because it widens access and economic opportunities for everyone. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the role explains the requirement.

x: Infrastructure widens access and opportunity, agricultural revival helps rural people, education improves capabilities, and health improves human capital. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each factor to its role.

x: Jobs let people share in growth, credit enables productive activity, SHGs bring financial participation, and MSMEs create jobs and entrepreneurs. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each factor to its role.

x: Economic development is a dimension of inclusive growth, governance means equal access to government facilities, shared benefits mean participation and inclusion, and cutting poverty and inequality is an objective. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Discriminate dimensions from objectives.

x: A is true and B is false: RTE brings disadvantaged children into the mainstream. Credit enables productive activity, while MSMEs provide jobs and entrepreneurship.
t: Match each factor to its role.

x: All four are linked to inclusive growth: infrastructure is a requirement, and education, health and credit each have a role in it.
t: Recall the elements of inclusive growth.

x: Governance and service delivery are part of inclusive governance, which aims at equal access to government facilities.
t: Match each element to its concept.

x: Shared economic benefits are a feature of inclusive growth: growth whose gains reach all sections.
t: Match each element to its concept.

x: Reducing poverty and inequality is an objective of inclusive growth. Infrastructure, MSMEs and SHGs are means to it.
t: Discriminate objectives from means.

x: Option C is incorrect: the working-age population is 15–64, not 16–64. Children below 15 and adults 65 and over are dependents.
t: Recall the age band 15–64.

x: The working-age population is 15–64, young dependents are below 15, old dependents 65 and over, and the demographic dividend is the gain from a larger working-age share. The answer is a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii.
t: Match each group to its age band.

x: Demographic transition runs from Stage I through Stage IV in order, so the answer is B, D, A, C.
t: Put the stages in number order.

x: Option C is incorrect: Stage II has a high birth rate and a falling death rate. A falling birth rate with a low death rate is Stage III.
t: Track birth and death rates stage by stage.

x: Stage I has high birth and death rates, Stage II a high birth rate and falling death rate, Stage III a falling birth rate and low death rate, and Stage IV low rates for both. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Track birth and death rates stage by stage.

x: The demographic dividend is the potential gain when the working-age share of the population is large, giving more possible workers.
t: Recall the demographic dividend.

x: The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook. The World Bank publishes the World Development Report, and the ILO the Global Wage Report.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: Option C is incorrect: the ILO, not the UNDP, publishes the Global Wage Report. The IMF publishes the GFSR, and the World Bank the WDR.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: I, II and III are correct: the World Bank publishes the WDR and published Ease of Doing Business, and the WEF publishes the Global Competitiveness Report. IV is false because the WEF publishes the Gender Gap Report.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: The World Economic Forum publishes the Travel & Tourism Competitiveness Report, as well as the Global Competitiveness and Gender Gap reports.
t: Recall the WEF reports.

x: The WEF publishes the Travel & Tourism Report. The ILO publishes the World Social Protection Report and the Global Wage Report, and the World Social Security Report was its earlier title. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: Both are true: the IMF publishes the Global Financial Stability Report, and UNFPA the State of World Population report.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: The UNDP publishes the HDI, the IMF the GFSR, the WEF the Competitiveness Report, and the ILO the Global Wage Report. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: Three are UNDP measures: the Human Development Report, the HDI and the Capability Poverty Measure. The Global Gender Gap Report is the WEF's.
t: Find the non-UNDP report.

x: The World Bank stopped the Ease of Doing Business report in 2021 after problems with its data. The HDR, GFSR and WDR still come out.
t: Recall the discontinued report.

x: The IMF publishes the WEO, the UNDP the Capability Poverty Measure, the ILO the World Social Protection Report, and UNFPA the State of World Population. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each report to its publisher.

x: Both are true: the World Social Security Report was the ILO's earlier title, later renamed the World Social Protection Report.
t: Recall the ILO report's renaming.

x: The World Economic Outlook is the WEO, the Global Financial Stability Report the GFSR, and the Human Development Report the HDR. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv.
t: Expand each short name.

x: The Human Development Index is the HDI, the Capability Poverty Measure the CPM, and the World Development Report the WDR. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-i.
t: Expand each short name.
